title: A scalable synthesis of silicon nanoparticles as high-performance anode material for lithium-ion batteries

lanes.label: Microscopy: SEM, HRTEM
lanes.sub: foundation model in hand or candidate

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Scalable wet milling plus centrifugation can bring Si below the ~150 nm fracture size, and removing the surface SiOx should raise capacity and first-cycle efficiency.
states.detail: Need: Si anodes offer high capacity but fracture on lithiation, and nano-Si routes do not scale. Design: commercial micrometre Si feedstock, wet bead milling with 0.3 mm YSZ beads in ethanol for up to 11 h at 1800 rpm, centrifugation at 11,000 rpm for 5 min, spray drying, then HF etching at 5 wt% for 30 min. Sweep: d50 = 628, 162, 126, 62 nm, and 62 nm as-received against HF-etched.

states.title: Size and phase state
states.head: Si nanoparticles with d50 = 62 nm and d99 = 147 nm, below the 150 nm fracture size, still single-phase fcc Si with broadened reflections from milling strain.
states.detail: Feature size (s10) rests on laser diffraction, the SEM count and the precedent that particles below ~150 nm do not fracture on lithiation (s16). Phase (s17) rests on XRD. No cycling-stability data test the fracture-size premise.

states.title: Surface state
states.head: As-received particles carry a ~3 nm amorphous SiOx shell and Zr traces from the milling media. HF etching removes both.
states.detail: Composition claim s19, resolved by HRTEM and EDX. The EDX oxygen signal only partly supports the removal.

states.title: Size-effect property state
states.head: Smaller unetched particles give lower initial capacity and lower first-cycle efficiency (2980 to 1485 mAh/g, 82 to 55%), because they carry relatively more SiOx and far more surface area for SEI (16 to 198 m2/g).
states.detail: Property s22 with mechanism s27. Crystalline Li15Si4 formation is suppressed for d50 at or below 162 nm (s25), argued from a 0.45 V plateau and the self-limiting lithiation precedent (s26).

states.title: Etching performance state
states.head: HF etching raises the 62 nm Si initial delithiation capacity from 1485 to 2801 mAh/g and first CE from 55.0 to 68.9%. The etched anode gives 2940/2801/2417 mAh/g at 0.01/0.05/0.10 C.
states.detail: Property s29, mechanism s32 (the SiOx shell slows Li+ and electron transport and consumes Li irreversibly), performance s33.

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Scalable milling and centrifugation give 62 nm Si, and HF removal of SiOx makes it a high-capacity anode.
states.detail: The framing that small is good sits in tension with the paper's own size series, where smaller is worse until etched.

nodes.title: SEM, Figure 4
nodes.head: Pristine Si is several-micrometre angular grains; milled Si is irregular platelets. A 150-particle SEM count gives 20 to 160 nm, mean ~80 nm, close to laser diffraction.
nodes.solves: Particle size and shape in the size state.
nodes.fm: SEM foundation model. Particle segmentation and a size histogram against the scale bar is the textbook task.
nodes.necessity_reason: Laser diffraction alone gives d50 = 62 nm.

nodes.title: SEM audit, Figure 4
nodes.head: The platelets in the micrograph measure 0.3 to 0.7 um against the 2 um bar, inconsistent with the 20 to 160 nm histogram. Either the count came from another field or the bar is misreported. Nothing supports 'no agglomerates'.
nodes.fm: An SEM model size read against the scale bar is exactly this test, and the answer is a number.
nodes.necessity_reason: Puts the 62 nm claim itself in doubt, and that claim is the premise of the fracture-size argument.

nodes.title: HRTEM, Figure 5
nodes.head: A ~3 nm amorphous rim on the as-received particle. The etched particle shows lattice fringes to the edge, with a ~1 nm disordered rim still visible.
nodes.fm: TEM candidates (EM-DINO, EMCF). Shell-thickness measurement from a lattice-resolved edge, with the residual 1 nm rim as the hard case.
nodes.note: The residual rim means removal is partial, which the EDX oxygen also says.
nodes.necessity_reason: Only strong evidence for the shell and its removal. EDX oxygen barely drops.

nodes.title: XRD, Figure 3
nodes.head: Nano-Si reflections are much weaker and broader than raw Si, with no extra phases.
nodes.solves: Phase in the size state: single fcc Si with lattice strain and reduced crystalline fraction.
nodes.fm: XRD models (Dara for phase identification, XtalNet or DiffractGPT for structure) can confirm single-phase Si. Crystallite size from peak width is classical Scherrer.
nodes.necessity_reason: No downstream node uses single-phase Si.

nodes.title: Laser PSD and BET, Fig 2, Table 1
nodes.head: d50 falls to 174 nm in 6 h, then plateaus near 126 nm by 11 h. Centrifugation narrows the PSD to a 0.1 um cut-off. BET rises from 16 to 198 m2/g as d50 falls to 62 nm.
nodes.detail: The milling-time trend (s11) was not opened and rests on caption and text. The PSD shift (s12) is shown in Figure 2. BET areas come from Table 1 (s28) and feed the surface-area mechanism in the size-effect state.
nodes.solves: Size in the size state and surface area in the size-effect state.
nodes.fm: No foundation model. Laser diffraction and BET are instrument outputs.
nodes.necessity_reason: Size series and BET carry the size-effect state.

nodes.title: EDX, Figure 5
nodes.head: Zr peaks (0.51 wt%) vanish after HF. Oxygen falls only from 6.42 to 4.55 wt%. Cu comes from the grid.
nodes.inner_audit: Oxygen largely persists after etching, so EDX does not support full SiOx removal. The text is silent on this.
nodes.fm: No foundation model. Line-library lookup and standardless quantification.
nodes.necessity_reason: HRTEM carries the surface state. EDX adds the Zr removal and the oxygen caveat.

nodes.title: Electrochemistry, Figs 6 to 8
nodes.head: First-cycle curves rank delithiation capacity 628 > 162 > 126 > 62 nm. A 0.45 V Li15Si4 plateau is clean only for 628 nm. Rate curves at 0.01/0.05/0.10 C fall with rate. CV of as-received Si shows activation over cycles 1 to 3 and an extra anodic peak near 0.25 V.
nodes.detail: Capacity ranking by size (s23), the Li15Si4 plateau read (s24, partial: the 126 and 162 nm curves also flatten near 0.42 V), Table 2 for as-received against etched capacity and CE (s30), the CV activation and extra peak (s31), and the rate series (s34).
nodes.solves: The size-effect state and the etching performance state.
nodes.op: read trend, read characteristic point, recognize signature
nodes.inner_audit: Every figure end point sits ~1.35x below the quoted delithiation capacity (for example 2050 against 2801 mAh/g). The constant factor suggests a different mass basis between figures and tables. Coulombic efficiency is unaffected. Text silent.
nodes.fm: No foundation model for charge-discharge curves at this scale. End points, plateaus and CV peaks are classical reads, and the 1.35x audit is a ratio.
nodes.necessity_reason: All capacity and CE numbers live here.
